control_flow: In followLine: if the line tracker reads below 30 %, curve left; else if it reads above 70 %, curve right; else drive straight at 20 %.

likely_intent.description: Follow the black line through its curves, without leaving it, and reach the green goal at the line's end.

decision_points.condition: first: the line tracker reads less than 30 %; second: the line tracker reads more than 70 %

branches.outcome: the line tracker reads below 30 % (black): it curves left
the line tracker reads above 70 % (white band or peach floor): it curves right

branches.reason: This reading happens only at the edge of the black line, a boundary, and only for a moment.
branches.outcome: the line tracker reads between 30 % and 70 %: it drives straight

input_dimensions.dimension: where the robot starts relative to the line

scenarios.coded_response: It curves left while the line tracker reads below 30 %, curves right while it reads above 70 %, and drives straight in between.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts on a black line that runs through curves, with a green goal at its end.
scenarios.trigger: The program starts and the line tracker sees the black core and the white band again and again.
scenarios.title: Follows the line through curves to the goal
assumptions: The green goal covers the line's end.
The line has curves that the robot can follow.
Staying on the line means keeping the line tracker on the black core or its white band.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It stays on the line through the curves and reaches the green goal at its end without leaving the line.

uncertainties: You didn't say what the robot should do if it starts beside the line or if there is no line.
The line tracker's reading between 30 % and 70 % happens only at the edge of the black line, for a moment: a boundary.
On a plain peach floor the line tracker reads about 83 %, so the program curves right without end.
